report.summary: The Astronomy Shop namespace is up (all 28 pods Running/Ready, 0 restarts at 02:43:16Z) but every PostgreSQL-backed path fails because the database server rejects the 'otelu' credential. Pod postgresql-6bd9b846cb-svkk2 logs 'FATAL: password authentication failed for user "otelu"' continuously from 02:42:52.250Z to 02:43:12.054Z. Consequently product-catalog's own ListProducts server span returns INTERNAL 'failed to load products: failed to query products: pq: password authentication failed for user "otelu"' and its postgresql client span fails with 'driver: bad connection'; product-reviews' own get_product_reviews span fails with psycopg2.OperationalError for the same reason; recommendation, checkout (PlaceOrder fails to get product 6E92ZMYYFZ), frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator all return their own 500/gRPC errors on the same traces. The database itself started cleanly and seeded data at 02:42:03-02:42:08Z (CREATE ROLE, INSERT 0 50 reviews, INSERT 0 10 products), so the catalog data exists; the clients simply cannot authenticate. The credential configuration changed during the incident window: Deployments accounting, product-catalog and product-reviews were updated by kubectl-set/kubectl-rollout between 02:42:47Z and 02:42:54Z (new ReplicaSets; product-catalog's DB_CONNECTION_STRING switched from an inline literal to secretKeyRef product-catalog-db-conn) and ConfigMap postgresql-init was patched (kubectl-patch) at 02:42:51Z to a password of 'otelp_7k9m2q4x', while Deployment postgresql was never touched after helm apply at 02:41:59Z and its pod (ephemeral data dir, init.sql executed only at container start) never restarted. Most likely mechanism (hypothesis): an otelu credential rotation was applied to the clients and to init.sql but never to the running database, which still holds the pre-rotation password. Which side holds the wrong value cannot be proven because the Secret and the redacted inline passwords cannot be read, so the exact object holding the offending credential remains unverified; the observed rejection originates at the postgresql database.

recommendation's own span get_product_list failed at 2026-11-24T02:43:04.776Z, and its client span oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts returned rpc.grpc.status_code=13 with status description 'failed to load products: failed to query products: pq: password authentication failed for user "otelu"'.

Kafka lag and container resource exhaustion are not supported as causes: no MessageConsumerLag or CPU-throttling alert was firing in the 02:43:27Z rules snapshot, no pod shows OOMKilled/Evicted/restart, and cart/valkey calls in the failing traces succeeded.

Reconcile the otelu password so that ConfigMap postgresql-init, Secret product-catalog-db-conn and the inline DB_CONNECTION_STRING values of accounting and product-reviews all carry the value the database actually holds, then restart the postgresql pod (its data directory is ephemeral, so init.sql is the only source of the role) and re-test product-catalog ListProducts, product-reviews GetProductReviews, recommendation and checkout.

Review who/what ran kubectl-set, kubectl-rollout, kubectl-patch and the 'administrator command' session on postgresql between 02:42:44Z and 02:42:56Z, and consider a persistent volume for postgresql so a credential change does not silently depend on a container restart.

gaps: Secret product-catalog-db-conn and the redacted credential values (product-catalog secretKeyRef value, accounting and product-reviews inline DB_CONNECTION_STRING passwords, postgresql POSTGRES_PASSWORD) could not be read, so the exact mismatched password values and which side (client or server) holds the wrong one are unverified.

The content of ConfigMap postgresql-init before the 02:42:51Z patch is not retained (metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives only the last write), so the pre-rotation otelu password is unknown, and the single 'terminating connection due to administrator command' backend at 02:42:56.068Z (possibly a pg_terminate_backend during a rotation) cannot be attributed.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who applied the kubectl-set/kubectl-rollout/kubectl-patch changes at 02:42:44-02:42:54Z and with which values is unknown.

No pre-incident baseline exists for these services: all 23 deployments were created at 02:41:59Z, Jaeger keeps only its newest traces in memory and the traces_span_metrics series had a single sample at 02:43:00Z, so no latency or error-rate trend before the fault can be established.

accounting's Deployment was updated (kubectl-set, 02:42:51Z) and its pod replaced, but no request reached it because checkout fails at the product lookup, so whether accounting would also fail authentication and whether it is impacted is unverified; it is a change during the window without observed impact.

checkout.astronomy-shop:8080 returned probe_success=0 at 02:43:13Z while its pod was Running/Ready; the probe definition and target could not be inspected, so the meaning of that probe failure is unknown.

No STATUS_CODE_ERROR series were returned from traces_span_metrics_calls_total for 02:20-02:43Z (the query returned no data, and only STATUS_CODE_UNSET/OK series were present), so metric-based error rates and any comparison against a baseline could not be computed.

product-catalog and product-reviews pod application logs contained no error lines for the window (product-catalog's product-catalog container had no log output; product-reviews logged only startup), so log-based confirmation came from the postgresql pod and from trace exception details.
next_steps: Compare the actual value in Secret product-catalog-db-conn and the inline DB_CONNECTION_STRING of accounting/product-reviews with the password in ConfigMap postgresql-init, then make them consistent.

If the new password is intended, restart the postgresql pod so init.sql re-creates the otelu role with it (the data directory is ephemeral), or run an ALTER USER otelu WITH PASSWORD as the postgres superuser.
Confirm with the platform owner what change was applied at 02:42:44-02:42:54Z (kubectl-set/kubectl-rollout/kubectl-patch/kubectl rollout restart) and why postgresql was excluded from it.
After the credential is aligned, re-check product-catalog ListProducts, product-reviews GetProductReviews, recommendation, checkout PlaceOrder and the load-generator failure ratio.
